emily (AE): Heads-up: Acme Corp procurement says they will issue purchase orders split across 3 legal entities. They want a single line-item seat commit and pro-rated invoices per entity. Marketplace UX only lets one billing entity. Can we support?

mike (SalesOps): Clarify: are they buying via marketplace marketplace (GCP/AWS) or want us to invoice them directly? That changes options.

emily (AE): They submitted marketplace intent but procurement insists on separate POs per entity for internal cost centers. They still want the commit discount applied at customer level.

jon (Billing): Marketplace behavior: invoices go to the payer account tied to marketplace. Multi-entity split on a single marketplace subscription isn't supported by the marketplace itself. We have 3 practical routes: 
- Option 1: Customer issues 3 marketplace POs, one per entity (each mapped to SKU lines) and we map commits proportionally.
- Option 2: Redwood invoices outside marketplace (direct invoicing) and we generate 3 separate invoices (manual split) and apply the commit discount across the sum.
- Option 3: One marketplace PO (single payer) + customer does internal chargebacks.

jon (Billing): Tradeoffs: Opt1 minimal manual work but procurement says they can't make 3 POs. Opt2 requires Legal + Deal Desk sign-off, accounting metadata per invoice (tax IDs, bill-to), and monthly reconciliation.

rachel (Legal): If we invoice outside marketplace we need an amendment to the MSSA to allow split billing / multi-invoice delivery and to confirm payment terms. Deal desk approval required for special invoicing. Also need payer/payee mappings in the SOW addendum.

oliver (GCP PM): On GCP marketplace specifically, commit discounts are applied at subscription level and cannot be split across three different billing entities. If they want the commit benefit and marketplace visibility, the only path is three marketplace subscriptions (painful).

katie (Customer): We can't create 3 POs. Internal process prohibits creating multiple POs for the same service. They asked if Redwood can accept one master contract and issue downstream invoices to each entity.

mike (SalesOps): Two concrete proposals to present to procurement: 
1) Redwood does direct invoicing outside marketplace and issues three monthly invoices, pro-rated by headcount. This requires Deal Desk + Finance sign-off and a one-time ops setup fee.
2) Keep marketplace subscription under one entity and Acme handles chargebacks internally (procurement to accept).

jon (Billing): If we go with direct invoicing we need the following on the PO/invoice request: 
```
- bill_to_name
- bill_to_address
- tax_id (EIN/VAT)
- contact email for AP
- invoice cadence (monthly/quarterly)
- sku mapping (SKU, qty, unit_price, term_start, term_end)
```
We also need the commit discount percentage to apply to the aggregated sum.

rachel (Legal): Also require a statement of work or schedule listing the three legal entities as receivers of the invoices and confirming acceptance of the net payment terms.

emily (AE): Customer asked what the deal desk approval timeline looks like. They want this sorted this week.

mike (SalesOps): I'll open the deal desk ticket. We need Revenue Ops for pricing approval (commit allocation), Finance for operational capacity, Legal for the amendment. Typical SLA is 2-3 business days if we have all artifacts.

emily (AE): Customer also asks about seat proration math — how we handle mid-term seat changes across entities.

jon (Billing): Proration approach if direct invoicing: compute total committed seats, apply discount to total, then prorate invoice amounts by entity headcount on each invoice date. Example formula: entity_amount = (entity_seats / total_seats) * (commit_price_after_discount) prorated by active days in period. We'll need headcount attestation from procurement.

katie (Customer): That math is fine. They want monthly invoices and a <30 day SLA for setup. Also asked if there is an additional charge for manual split invoicing.

jon (Billing): Manual setup + monthly admin is non-zero. Ballpark: 4 hours one-time setup + ~1 hour/month reconciliation. Recommend a one-time ops handling fee of $500 to cover initial mapping and template invoices. Need to include this as a line in the SOW or PO.

rachel (Legal): Legal ok with the amendment language (30 day net, invoice receivers listed). We need copies of the POs and the tax IDs to attach.

mike (SalesOps): Action plan: 
- I will create Deal Desk ticket with pricing: 12-mo commit, 5% commit discount applied at customer total, $500 ops fee for split invoicing, monthly cadence.
- Jon to confirm required invoice metadata and sample invoice format.
- Rachel to draft amendment template and SOW schedule.
- Emily to get procurement confirmation on exact AP contacts + tax IDs and confirm acceptance of the ops fee.

dealdesk-bot: Ticket created: DD-2024-6731 — link: https://redwood.ai/dealdesk/DD-2024-6731

mike (SalesOps): We should list approval owners in ticket: Revenue Ops (price), Finance (ops fee), Legal (amendment). I'll aim to have routing started today.

oliver (GCP PM): Heads-up: if they insist on staying in GCP marketplace but want commit applied, they'll need 3 subscriptions or we move them off-marketplace and use direct billing (which they seem to prefer we do).

katie (Customer): Procurement: we prefer direct invoices from Redwood if you can do the split and keep the commit discount. Please proceed with deal desk process.

emily (AE): I'll collect POs and tax IDs and post here by EOD tomorrow. Target: Deal Desk sign-off by Friday COB. :thumbsup:

mike (SalesOps): On it, I'll tag Revenue Ops and Finance in the ticket.

jon (Billing): Once deal desk approves, I'll create invoice templates and a sample monthly run for them to approve before live billing.

rachel (Legal): I'll attach the amendment draft to the deal desk ticket.

emily (AE): Thanks all — keeping procurement looped.

(emoji reactions): :white_check_mark: emily, :eyes: jon, :rocket: mike
